note: The frog's voice (doc 17 'pulse-croak', doc 25 'Creature voices'; src/audio/voices.js). Kept here until the frog work settles, then moved into recipes/species/frog.json as its voice field at merge (docs/audio-future-work.md). The common frog's call is a soft, low, purring croak, not a bullfrog, so this is gentle and slightly grainy. SOUND: a band-limited pulse train (harmonics partials, each k^-tilt, so it stays soft) repeating at a rate in rateHz (18 to 40 Hz) around baseRateHz, through two resonant bandpass formants (hz, q, db; near 600 Hz and 1.4 kHz) and a soft lowpass at lowpassHz; a little breath noise (breathDb) goes through the same formants. grain shakes each pulse's level (depth, from noise lowpassed at hz) and jitter wobbles its timing (cents, at hz), which is what makes it purr rather than buzz. PHRASE: each call is groups pulse groups (2 to 6, picked per call), each groupS long with gapS between, the pulse rate rising by rateRise across a group; attackS and releaseS round each group; groupAmp is the level of the first, second and later groups, so a phrase leans in and falls away. onsetS is the delay from the call start to the first pulse; the call start is when the game starts swelling the throat sac (recipes/species/frog.json motion.call.pulseS, 0.32 s), so the first group peaks while the sac is full. LEVEL: levelDb at intensity 1, intensityDb from intensity 0 to 1. INDIVIDUAL: each frog (its id hashed with the world seed) keeps a pitch offset within pitch (0.15 = plus or minus 15 percent, moving the formants and a little of the pulse rate) and a rhythm within rhythm (0.2 = plus or minus 20 percent, faster pulses and shorter groups together). SEASONS (doc 25): rate is the call density factor the behaviour applies (spring 1.3, summer 1, autumn 0.5, winter 0, silent); pitch multiplies the formants (autumn 5 percent lower); phrase multiplies how many groups (autumn shorter). The spring purr is a quiet low layer of distant callers under the chorus: a slow pulse train lowpassed at lowpassHz through a band at bandHz, two of them spread left and right (widthCents apart), at db when calls arrive at activityCallsPerS, rising and falling with recent calls over attackS and releaseS, and only in spring (by the spring weight). SPATIAL (doc 17): each call is its own placed voice, inverse distance from refDistance 2 m, rolloff 1, an air-absorption lowpass from 18 kHz at 2 m to 3 kHz at 60 m, and on mobile a gentle lowpass toward behind.hz when the frog is behind the view. maxVoices: at most this many calls sound at once, nearest first (a far call is dropped, or the farthest stopped, when full).
